definition.en: Whether a crease pattern can be folded all the way flat, every crease at ±180°, without the paper stretching, tearing or passing through itself. At one vertex it is decided by Maekawa's and Kawasaki's conditions; for a whole pattern it also depends on the stacking order of the layers.
definition.es: Si un patrón de pliegues puede doblarse hasta quedar completamente plano, con cada pliegue a ±180°, sin que el papel se estire, se rasgue ni se atraviese a sí mismo. En un vértice lo deciden las condiciones de Maekawa y de Kawasaki; en un patrón completo depende además del orden en que se apilan las capas.
definition.fr: Le fait qu'un canevas de plis puisse être plié complètement à plat, chaque pli à ±180°, sans que le papier s'étire, se déchire ou se traverse lui-même. En un sommet, les conditions de Maekawa et de Kawasaki en décident ; pour un canevas entier, l'ordre d'empilement des couches compte aussi.
definition.pt: Se um padrão de vincos pode ser dobrado até ficar completamente plano, com cada vinco a ±180°, sem que o papel estique, rasgue ou se atravesse a si mesmo. Num vértice decidem-no as condições de Maekawa e de Kawasaki; num padrão inteiro depende também da ordem em que as camadas se empilham.

constraints: Local conditions are necessary, not sufficient: a pattern whose every vertex passes Maekawa and Kawasaki can still be impossible to fold flat because of layer order, and deciding global flat-foldability is NP-hard. Never report a pattern flat-foldable from vertex checks alone.
sources: Thomas C. Hull, Origametry: Mathematical Methods in Paper Folding, Cambridge University Press, 2020
Erik D. Demaine and Joseph O'Rourke, Geometric Folding Algorithms: Linkages, Origami, Polyhedra, Cambridge University Press, 2007
Marshall Bern and Barry Hayes, "The complexity of flat origami", Proceedings of the 7th ACM-SIAM Symposium on Discrete Algorithms (SODA), 1996
